The correct starting material for synthesizing 5-isopropyl-3,4-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene via ring-closing metathesis (RCM) is a terminal diene that can form a six-membered ring with the appropriate substituents in the correct positions.  

RCM of a 1,7-octadiene forms a cyclohexene ring by connecting C-2 and C-7 and losing ethylene. The substituents on the ring correspond to the groups attached to C-3, C-4, and C-5 of the diene. The product requires a methyl at C-3, a methyl at C-4, and an isopropyl at C-5 of the cyclohexene ring.  

Option (A) is 5-isopropyl-3,4-dimethylocta-1,7-diene. Its structure has double bonds at C-1/C-2 and C-7/C-8, placing the methyl groups on C-3 and C-4 and the isopropyl group on C-5. RCM would yield exactly cyclohexene with methyls at positions 3 and 4 and an isopropyl at position 5. The other options do not have the correct diene geometry, substitution pattern, or chain length to give the desired product.  

Answer: A

The reaction joins the two alkene carbons that are part of the diene termini, forming a new double bond between them and releasing the other fragments.
